correctness.rationale: The star triangle bound makes all leaf-pair constraints redundant. The residual description has interior at zero and each of the fibers at fixed center t has two distinct endpoints per leaf because ρ_i>0. Arm strips with ρ_i≥2 follow from the cube; for the remaining facet inequalities I checked the strict witnesses in the proof: near a center cap choose leaves slightly toward the interior, for a leaf cap use t=1−ρ_i/2 when ρ_i<2 and t=0 otherwise, and for a tight strip use t=−ρ_i/2 with the distinguished leaf at ρ_i/2. Negation handles opposite signs. Every vertex must use one endpoint per coordinate; at an endpoint t=±1 the center is pinned and all fiber corners have full active rank. At an interior corner without a doubly active chosen endpoint, all chosen endpoints are affine near t and admit a two-sided perturbation. At a doubly active endpoint its cap and strip determine t, and the other endpoint equations determine all leaves, so the point is extreme. If one leaf can pin t using either endpoint, every corner qualifies; otherwise precisely 2^(m−s(t)) corners avoid all pins. Counting at most 2m events of 2^(m−1) corners each proves the sharp maximum, and the claimed generic conditions separate those events. In a signed objective, use the upper endpoint for a positive coefficient and the lower endpoint for a negative coefficient. This produces a continuous concave piecewise-affine function; its slopes and all interior breakpoints give the stated exact formula and O(m log m) sweep, with ρ_i=2 contributing no interior event. The frozen support was inspected, not executed; the dimension-uniform conclusions follow analytically.

evidence: Gordon–Petrov’s universal face-vector theorem requires generic strict metrics. Hille–Theewis discuss general extremality and norming sets, including Farmer’s extremality results.

Hille–Theewis’s exact optimization for positive atomic ν versus positive μ already covers arbitrary signed atomic input by Jordan decomposition, and their finite-support formulation is an LP. Their scalar threshold formulas concern a single Dirac against a positive measure.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The face-vector theorem does not cover the augmented star family for m≥2. The general descriptions supply machinery but do not give this collision enumeration, sharp count, or the particular one-variable formula for signed measures with multiple atoms on both sides. The latter should not be presented as the first exact algorithm for arbitrary signed FM norms.

evidence: The generic-strict face formula covers a three-point strict metric (including the compatible one-arm case 0<ρ<2), not the forced equalities in larger stars.

The retrieved general extreme-point and atomic optimization statements do not spell out star-specific counts or their behavior at collisions; the LP is a representation from which some elementary specializations can be made.

The reviewed breakpoint objective can also be maximized by weighted selection of its nonnegative slope drops at cumulative weight equal to the initial slope. This yields a linear-time option in the same model, without contradicting the asserted upper bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: What survives these reductions is the explicit all-parameter enumeration and treatment of degeneracies, not the abstract existence of an optimization or a sorting-based algorithm. The hard hypothesis mismatch for m≥2 prevents obtaining the claimed vertex counts by substitution in the generic strict theorem.

evidence: Resultary c1fad2fa9990 uses the same type of star and signed measures, but imposes ‖f‖∞+Lip(f)≤1 and optimizes over two scalar parameters.
The max-type constraint is equivalent to a pointed Lipschitz polytope with a new point at distance 1 from every existing point and original distances capped at 2.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The sum and max constraints give different norms even for one arm: with ρ≥2, the max constraint allows endpoint difference 2, while minimizing the sum-norm cost for difference Δ gives |Δ|/2+|Δ|/ρ, hence maximal difference 2ρ/(ρ+2). The apex reformulation is equivalent, but for two or more leaves it forces a triangle equality, through the hub if the two arm lengths sum to at most 2 and through the apex otherwise.

originality.rationale: The supported increment is the all-length weighted-star face/vertex classification, including a collision count and exact attainable maximum, together with a one-coordinate breakpoint formula for the maximum-type norm on this geometry. General extreme-point and FM optimization theory are antecedents. The strongest same-day weighted-star result found treats the sum norm, not an equivalent copy of this polytope or norm formula. The sweep bound is valid but is not a claim of optimality or the source of the main structural novelty.

value.rationale: These stars are a natural nongeneric family of pointed Lipschitz polytopes. Knowing exactly which fiber corners remain extreme when lengths coincide, become complementary, hit one or two, or exceed two gives useful all-parameter information that a generic face vector or general LP does not deliver. It also yields a short evaluation rule for arbitrary signed data with no equal-mass condition. The main value is the exact classification and degeneracy analysis, not a claim of an optimal sweep or of a new general FM solver.
